info.title: mendel-api
info.summary: The forge and Mendel, over one schema.
info.description: **The schema is the contract.** `frontend/src/api/` is generated from this document and never hand-edited, and an agent driving Mendel reads the same document — so an operation without an `operationId`, a tag, or a declared refusal is a gap in both consumers at once.

a directory — conflating the two makes a liveness probe do real work.

get.summary: What the registry in use holds
Whether the AI lane can do anything, and what is waiting
get.description:
**Three things an operator checks when a generation is not happening**, and the plan
names all three: worker unavailable, model unavailable, queue depth.

It reports and never enqueues. A health endpoint that started work to find out whether work
can start is a health endpoint that changes the thing it measures.

get.summary: Every landed contract, for the picker
get.description:
**Every contract, not only the ones in a pipeline.**

The builder's left panel is a picker you drag from; a list containing only what is already on
the canvas is a table of contents. `GET /tools` answers a different question — *what is the
state of everything* — and carries drift, drafts and undrafted tools, none of which can be

post.summary: Is this graph legal, and what is unmet or unconventional about it
post.description:
**200 whatever it finds.**

A verdict is the answer, not an error: a person mid-gesture would rather see three problems
than the first one, and the forge's `verify` ladder is the precedent. Refusal lives at
`keep` and at the emission gates, which is the boundary the spec draws.

An unknown contract comes back as an `MD0509` finding rather than a 422 — a draft naming a
contract that has since been renamed is a thing to be told about on the canvas, not an
error that empties the screen.

get.summary: What can feed what, so a browser can colour a wire without a round trip
get.description:
The client looks up; it never decides. See `mendel_resolver.compatibility`.

`ETag` is the registry digest — the same string that invalidates the server's own cache, so
"the registry changed" has one definition rather than two. A reload becomes a 304 instead of
the whole table.

304.description: the registry has not changed since your copy

get.summary: What could sit on the other end of a wire, in the resolver's own order
get.description:
The port picker's ordering, and the reason beside each row.

**Filtering is the browser's; ordering is not.** `GET /pipeline/compatibility` already tells a
client what fits — that is a lookup it can do without a round trip, and `useCompatibility`
does. What it cannot know is which candidate `resolve()` would reach for, and that is what
makes the picker an answer rather than a filtered list.

`states` is a comma-separated list, empty for none. A **query** rather than a path segment
because a state set is unordered and a path implies one.

`side=producing` asks *what could feed this input*; `side=consuming` asks *what would accept
this output*. Only the first has the resolver's authority behind its order, and
`services/candidates.py` says so rather than pretending otherwise.

get.summary: Every pipeline this lab has
get.description:
The *by pipeline* half of the front door — and **it had no query at all** until Plan 4
phase 2. The build router carried create, read, save, keep and bundle, every one addressed
by a known id; nothing could answer *what do we have*.

**Readiness, never history.** A run's outcome belongs to `wiener-api` and to the *by run*
view; leaking one onto a pipeline row is the defect `ov-work` names by hand.

**Nothing here resolves.** Provenance is read off the artifact `keep` wrote.

get.summary: The kept pipeline, as a zip somebody else can run
get.description:
**Mendel's half of the courier, and the whole of what it knows about running** — A179.

`docs/design/wiener.md` §12: the browser fetches this and posts it to Wiener, so the copy
happens in a place that can see both halves and neither half can see the other. This route
does not know that Wiener exists, has no idea what will be done with the archive, and would
serve the same bytes to `curl`.

**It does not check that a gate passed.** Whether an un-gated pipeline may run is a policy
about running, and running is Wiener's — `execution-boundary.md` §3. What Mendel owes here
is an honest artifact; the builder's own control is what refuses to offer the button before
a gate has passed, where a person can read the reason.

post.summary: Lay out a hand-drawn graph, in the shape the canvas already renders
post.description:
**Layout stays in Python.** `CLAUDE.md`: the DAG layout is computed server-side so the
canvas is as deterministic as the emitted `.nf`. A drawn graph gets the same treatment — a
browser laying out its own nodes would be the one part of the picture that could differ
between two people looking at the same pipeline.

Returns a `BuiltPipeline`, which is what `/pipeline` already returns, so Plan 3C's canvas
draws a hand-drawn graph without a component changing.

post.summary: Gate a kept draft
post.description:
Queue a gate and return immediately with a `queued` run.

A stub gate is up to 900s cold and nothing that long may sit in a request — `worker.py`'s
docstring has said so since phase 8.

**This is not *Run pipeline*.** A gate proves the artifact on public test data; running a
laboratory's data is Wiener's, and Mendel has no route for it by design.

AgentAsk.title: AgentAsk
AgentAsk.description: A question the agent put to the person, and how it is answered (#463).

AgentCommand.title: AgentCommand
AgentCommand.description:
A command the agent suggests for the run's shell (#511). A read-only one the Console runs on
the agent's behalf; any other only the person runs.

AgentMessage.title: AgentMessage
AgentMessage.description:
What the builder agent says, in its own words (#463). `narration` is what it said beside a
tool call, while working (#504): drawn with its trail, not as its answer.

AiHealth.title: AiHealth
AiHealth.description:
Three separate facts, because they fail separately and are fixed separately.

**A single `ok` would be the wrong shape.** No worker is a compose problem, no model is a
`.env` problem, and a queue with eleven things in it is neither — it is the system working.
Collapsing them gives an operator a red light and no next step, which is what §7's *honest
empty and error states* is about one layer down.

AnalysisDataView.title: AnalysisDataView
AnalysisDataView.description:
An analysis's data as the Data pages read it: everything but the file list, which is paged
(`files` is its count).

AnswerQuestion.title: AnswerQuestion
AnswerQuestion.description: The person's answer to the agent's question.

Artifact.title: Artifact
Artifact.description: A kept pipeline, as the document it is.

AtRunFactView.title: AtRunFactView
AtRunFactView.description: One fact a run-time setting reads, and where each sample's value comes from (#466).

AtRunView.title: AtRunView
AtRunView.description:
A setting decided at run time, as the card shows it before the run (#217, #466): the
facts it reads and where they come from, every row as a line, and what it is when no row
applies.

Author.title: Author
Author.description: Who made a choice in the goal: a person, or the builder agent (#463).

AuthoringCallView.title: AuthoringCallView
AuthoringCallView.description: One model call in the session, for the call panel (#182, #191).

AuthoringChanged.title: AuthoringChanged
AuthoringChanged.description: The person's change, recorded, and the session as it now is.

AuthoringPreview.title: AuthoringPreview
AuthoringPreview.description: The draft as `pipeline.yml` would read — **a preview, never the kept artifact.**

AuthoringSessionView.title: AuthoringSessionView
AuthoringSessionView.description: Everything needed to restore the page, from one read.

AuthoringUsage.title: AuthoringUsage
AuthoringUsage.description: What the session's model calls have cost so far — the header's count (#191).

AuthoringVocabulary.title: AuthoringVocabulary
AuthoringVocabulary.description: Every declared type and its states, and who can measure each measurement.

BeginAuthoring.title: BeginAuthoring
BeginAuthoring.description:
What somebody wants, in their own words. **Prose, and nothing else**: a body that took a
model id would let a browser choose what a provider is sent to.

Call.title: Call
Call.description: One thing asking for a person: how much, said plainly, and where it lives.

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description: One contract that could go here, and why it is where it is in the list.

ChangeAuthoring.title: ChangeAuthoring
ChangeAuthoring.description: The person's change to what is wanted, what they have, a fact, a tool or a setting.

Channel.title: Channel
Channel.description: One input or output as `meta.yml` describes it.

ChannelView.title: ChannelView
ChannelView.description:
One channel the pipeline reads from outside, as the canvas draws it.

═══ THE SEAM SPEC §12.3 FOUND, AND WHY IT IS A TASK ══════════════════════════════════════

§0's finding was that **the canvas already disagreed with the artifact**: it derived one
socket per unwired *port* — five on the spine, three of them `annotation.gtf` — while
`goal_of` deduplicated by type and the emitted workflow had one `params.gtf`. Nothing was
wrong on screen until somebody tried to name them.

Part A fixed the registry and Part B fixes the resolver, and **nothing said the API
changed** — so `Sources.entryChannels()` in the browser would have gone on computing its own
answer from unwired ports, and the canvas and the resolver would disagree *again*, in a new
way, because now there genuinely are named channels for it to disagree with.

So the browser stops deriving and starts reading. `entryChannels` is **deleted**, not left
beside this: two derivations of one fact is the defect this whole plan started from, and
keeping the old one "for now" is how it survives.

**It is also what makes phase 3's split/merge possible at all** — you cannot split a thing
that is recomputed from scratch on every render.

CommandBody.title: CommandBody
CommandBody.description:
A person's command. **There is no `actor` field**: the route sets it, so a body cannot
claim to be the AI or anyone else.

Compatibility.title: Compatibility
Compatibility.description: Serializable lookup tables for interactive port compatibility checks.

ConsoleContext.title: ConsoleContext
ConsoleContext.description: What the page carries from Run → Console with the person's words.

Constraints-Input.title: Constraints
Constraints-Input.description: The complete closed set of routing and parameter choices in a goal.

Constraints-Output.title: Constraints
Constraints-Output.description: The complete closed set of routing and parameter choices in a goal.

Counts.title: Counts
Counts.description:
What each choice would show given the other filters: a facet leaves out its own pick, so
its numbers stay choices rather than collapsing to the one already made. `reads` and `makes`
narrow each other, which is what lets a person follow one format.

Coverage.title: Coverage
Coverage.description: How much of the data a measured fact was read from (#465).

DataProfile.title: DataProfile
DataProfile.description:
Measured properties of the input data.

The record list gives published payloads declared keys. Person-authored goal files may use a
concise measurement-to-value mapping, which the pre-validator converts to records.

Production callers should build profiles through ``MeasurementRegistry.profile()`` so values
are also checked against their measurement declarations.

DataSample.title: DataSample
DataSample.description: One sample: its files (paths, read 1 first) and what was measured on it.

DataSummary.title: DataSummary
DataSummary.description: An analysis's data at a glance, for its card on Home (#511).

DecisionChange.title: DecisionChange
DecisionChange.description:
One change to intent or facts, from any caller — the person's click or edit, the chat
model's reply, a stage's own handler (Part I.0 spec §5.1). `heard` is the person's words it
was taken from, already checked (`heard.find`); `retract` removes what `subject` names.

Designed.title: Designed
Designed.description: Designed, not built: shown so the menu tells the truth about what is coming.

DomainView.title: DomainView
DomainView.description:
What values a setting accepts, so the card can render the right control.

`dashboard.md` §5: *parameters with alternatives render as a `<select>`; free values as an
input*. Without this the browser cannot tell one from the other and every setting is a text
box — including `index_format`, whose two legal values are `bai` and `csi`.

`None` on a setting means the contract declares no domain, which is legal and is what most
contracts say. A param whose legal values genuinely cannot be enumerated — `seq_platform`,
deliberately — declares none, and gets a free input.

DraftChannel.title: DraftChannel
DraftChannel.description:
Sockets explicitly grouped into one input channel.

Unlisted ports retain the default one-channel-per-type behavior.

DraftEdge.title: DraftEdge
DraftEdge.description: One wire: where it starts, where it ends. Nothing derived.

DraftIn.title: DraftIn
DraftIn.description: What a client sends to open or update a draft.

DraftLabel.title: DraftLabel
DraftLabel.description:
Private canvas label for one socket.

Labels never rename channel keys, parameters, samplesheet columns, or Nextflow variables and
do not reach the materialised IR or published artifact.

DraftParam.title: DraftParam
DraftParam.description:
A safe parameter value and optional reason entered in the builder.

The client does not assign provenance or tier; materialisation derives those trusted fields.

DraftRow.title: DraftRow
DraftRow.description:
One pipeline on the front door's *by pipeline* table.

**Readiness, not history** — `ov-work`. A run's outcome belongs to the *by run* view, and
leaking `last run 2d ago · M. Silva` onto a pipeline card is the actual bug that made two
blocks read as one list rendered twice.

DraftSave.title: DraftSave
DraftSave.description: A checked save; omitting graph permits a metadata-only rename.

DraftsPage.title: DraftsPage
DraftsPage.description: A page of the lab's pipelines, and the total behind it.

EditAuthoringDraft.title: EditAuthoringDraft
EditAuthoringDraft.description: The canvas as the person left it: the server reads what changed and records it.

Effect.title: Effect
Effect.description: Whether a decision changes step presence, implementation, or a parameter.

EmittedPipeline.title: EmittedPipeline
EmittedPipeline.description: The draft's Nextflow: what *Compile it* shows (one builder plan 5).

EnvItem.title: EnvItem
EnvItem.description: A locked collection record assembled from declared environment variables.

Evidence.title: Evidence
Evidence.description: How much input an inspector read to establish a measurement.

Fact.title: Fact
Fact.description: One thing gathering learned, and who it came from. Nothing is guessed (protocol rule 5).

FactRule.title: FactRule
FactRule.description: A decision that reads this fact: which role it fills, and its rows.

FactSetting.title: FactSetting
FactSetting.description: A setting worked out from this fact, as a formula a person reads.

FactSource.title: FactSource
FactSource.description: Where a fact came from, which is what the goal card and the tier-3 premise show.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: One declared diagnostic with optional node, port, and edge-endpoint context.

Fired.title: Fired
Fired.description: A matched row with its value, tier, justification, and layer evidence.

Fits.title: Fits
Fits.description:
Registry tools sharing a file format with a module. By format only, so a suggestion of
where it might go rather than a checked connection: its types are not decided yet.

Gate.title: Gate
Gate.description:
Validation checks, ordered from linting to execution on test data.

LINT runs Nextflow's linter on the generated workflow.
PREVIEW previews the workflow without executing its processes.
STUB runs the workflow using substitute process commands.
TEST runs the actual tools with test data.

GateIn.title: GateIn
GateIn.description:
**A gate, and nothing else.**

`docs/design/execution-boundary.md` §3: the test for whether something is a *run* rather
than a *gate* is whether it takes a samplesheet, and this cannot. No path, no output
directory, no input — `extra="forbid"` is what keeps it that way as the type grows.

GateView.title: GateView
GateView.description:
What the browser polls.

No path and no host detail — the same restraint the drafts routes take, for the same
reason. `output` is a tool's own text and is shown to the person who asked; see
`models.GateRun` for why it must not travel any further than that.

Goal-Input.title: Goal
Goal-Input.description: The resolver input, combining desired outputs with known input facts.

Goal-Output.title: Goal
Goal-Output.description: The resolver input, combining desired outputs with known input facts.

GoalInput-Input.title: GoalInput
GoalInput-Input.description: One available input, described by type, optional channel name, and states.

GoalInput-Output.title: GoalInput
GoalInput-Output.description: One available input, described by type, optional channel name, and states.

Grain.title: Grain
Grain.description:
How many items a channel carries relative to the analysis, and what a fact is about
(#466): one for the whole study, one per sample, or a part of one sample's item between a
splitter and its merger. Groups and lanes are declared on ports and channels instead (`by`,
`Channel.units`).

GuardView.title: GuardView
GuardView.description:
The samples a step takes when each sample's tool is chosen per sample (#466): the
tools whose samples come here, in a sentence, and the rule as the card shows a lookup.

InputChoice.title: InputChoice
InputChoice.description:
A person's choice for one optional input of one tool. Like `SourcePin`, it is the
person's by being in the goal's constraints, so it carries no `by`.

InputRule.title: InputRule
InputRule.description:
One of the tool's rules between its inputs and settings (#460, #511), said in words, with
whether this step as it is set up breaks it — so the Step tab can lay optional inputs out by
what they need, block and come in groups of.

InputState.title: InputState
InputState.description:
Whether a tool's optional input is part of the pipeline (#460).

`off` leaves it out. `optional` makes it a pipeline input each run may supply or leave
empty. `required` makes every run supply it, or wires it from another step.

Level.title: Level
Level.description: Severity and workflow meaning of a review finding.

Looks.title: Looks
Looks.description: How many of a folder's files are of one kind, by extension (`kinds.looks_like`).

Measured.title: Measured
Measured.description:
One measurement and where its value came from.

Generated entries record their measurer; a bare person-authored value is asserted.

Measurement.title: Measurement
Measurement.description: A typed property that a goal may assert or a measurer may measure.

MeasurerView.title: MeasurerView
MeasurerView.description: One way a measurement can be measured, and where that runs (#134).

MetaValue.title: MetaValue
MetaValue.description: Translate one declared value to the value expected in module metadata.

ModuleView.title: ModuleView
ModuleView.description:
A contract the left panel offers, for dragging onto the canvas.

**Every landed contract, not only the ones in this pipeline.** The first cut of the builder
listed the pipeline's own steps, which is a table of contents rather than a picker — you
cannot drag a module in from a list that only contains what is already there.

**There is no description, and the registry has nowhere to put one.** `ModuleContract` has no
`summary` field and `priority_because` is empty on all twelve shipped contracts, so the card
shows what a contract actually knows: its roles, what it needs, what it makes, and its
container. The prose the design's card shows would need a registry schema change — issue #78.

Needs.title: Needs
Needs.description: Something else has to be set first.

NfTest.title: NfTest
NfTest.description: One nf-test case and the `test-datasets` paths it reads.

Notice.title: Notice
Notice.description:
A refusal, or the agent stopping at its limit.

`code` carries a diagnostic rather than a provider's sentence — `GateFailure`'s lesson, one
level up: machine-generated text is the likeliest leak precisely because nobody wrote it and
nobody reads it.

NoticeKind.title: NoticeKind
NoticeKind.description:
What a `notice` is about.

`REFUSAL` is where a provider's failure
surfaces, and it carries a code rather than a provider's message for `GateFailure`'s reason.

OfferContext.title: OfferContext
OfferContext.description: What the frame was drawn against, so a stale frame is recognisable.

OpenValue.title: OpenValue
OpenValue.description: One tier-4 value nobody has answered, named.

ParamOverride.title: ParamOverride
ParamOverride.description:
A validated human parameter override.

The closed value type prevents arbitrary path-bearing values from entering a goal.

PartsView.title: PartsView
PartsView.description:
A step that can run on parts of each sample (#466): whether it does, the tools that split
and merge, and why. Shown whether it is on or kept whole, so the card offers the switch.

PersonConsole.title: PersonConsole
PersonConsole.description: What the person saw on Run → Console when they wrote (#511), beside their words.

Pinned.title: Pinned
Pinned.description: A value in `.env` beats every layer. The variable is named so a person knows where to go.

PortView.title: PortView
PortView.description:
One port of a step, as the canvas draws it.

**A port is a dot** — `dashboard.md` §3, which records that a five-shape family code was
removed because *an encoding that needs its legend on screen at all times is a lookup rather
than an encoding*. Two channels survive because each is binary and each means something a
reader acts on: **hollow** when a required input is unmet, **doubled** when it accepts many.
The type is text, on hover.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Why part of a module could not be read. `code` is an `MF05xx` diagnostic.

ProducerExclusion-Input.title: ProducerExclusion
ProducerExclusion-Input.description:
A producer excluded at one site.

The router uses another candidate or reports a conflict when none remains.

ProducerExclusion-Output.title: ProducerExclusion
ProducerExclusion-Output.description:
A producer excluded at one site.

The router uses another candidate or reports a conflict when none remains.

ProducerPin-Input.title: ProducerPin
ProducerPin-Input.description:
A person's producer choice at a routing site.

The router applies it before rules and records a differing choice as a human override.

ProducerPin-Output.title: ProducerPin
ProducerPin-Output.description:
A person's producer choice at a routing site.

The router applies it before rules and records a differing choice as a human override.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description:
How much of one pipeline was settled without judgement — a proportion of one whole.

**Read from the stored artifact, never from a re-resolve.** The 2026-08-19 audit found every
registry-touching screen cost ~250ms warm and one function was responsible; a front door that
rebuilt four pipelines to draw four bars would be that finding arriving again, this time on
the page a person opens first.

`settled` is tiers 1 and 2 — **tier 3 is deliberately not in it.** A rule matched measured
data, which is the machinery working, and the premise behind the measurement still needs a
person. `frontend/src/build/Provenance.tsx` says the same thing in the same words, and
counting tier 3 as settled would turn the one element carrying the product's claim into the
one element overstating it.

Reader.title: Reader
Reader.description:
**A reader and what it measures** (Registry · Measurers, board 7b): a format our code reads
as data is read, or a tool's output read in the run; each fact it makes, the rules and settings
that decide by it, and its tests.

Reference.title: Reference
Reference.description: A study-wide file (a genome, an annotation), named with its type by the person.

Refusal.title: Refusal
Refusal.description: A coded refusal. `detail` is `"<code>: <message>"` — `forge explain <code>` expands it.

Replayed.title: Replayed
Replayed.description: One past decision the proposed rows would have settled, and whether the same way.

RequiredStates.title: RequiredStates
RequiredStates.description:
A wanted output type and the states it must carry.

The record form keeps payload keys declared and validated. ``Constraints`` still accepts a
mapping shorthand when reading person-authored goal files.

ReviewAiChoices.title: ReviewAiChoices
ReviewAiChoices.description: The steps whose AI choices the person has looked at, or all of them.

RoleAbsence.title: RoleAbsence
RoleAbsence.description: A role disabled by a person, excluding every contract that fills it.

RuleView.title: RuleView
RuleView.description: One decision of a role this tool fills. A rule belongs to a role, not a tool.

SampleFact.title: SampleFact
SampleFact.description: One fact measured on one uploaded sample (#466).

SayToAuthoring.title: SayToAuthoring
SayToAuthoring.description: Words to the agent. **No revision**: saying something changes nothing by itself.

ScannedFile.title: ScannedFile
ScannedFile.description: One file in a ticked folder, and what it turned out to be.

SettingView.title: SettingView
SettingView.description:
One resolved parameter, as the settings card needs it.

**Editable since Plan 3E.** It was read-only in 3C, and the field was absent rather than
disabled on the argument that a box which looks typeable and discards what you type is worse
than a value that says it is a record. That was right while nothing persisted an edit;
`DraftParam` is now somewhere to put the answer.

Shown.title: Shown
Shown.description: What a server may say about a value. For a secret, `value` is always `None`.

Site-Input.title: Site
Site-Input.description: A routing location identified by output type and required states.

Site-Output.title: Site
Site-Output.description: A routing location identified by output type and required states.

SourcePin.title: SourcePin
SourcePin.description: A person's choice of producer for one consumer port.

StepView.title: StepView
StepView.description:
One step, as a canvas needs it — **not the whole `Step`.**

A `Step` carries its module digest, its container and its include path, none of which a node
on a canvas draws. Sending them anyway would make the payload three times the size for a
screen that shows a name and a tier.

Strip.title: Strip
Strip.description: What the registry in use holds.

TierCard.title: TierCard
TierCard.description: One tier, as an interface needs to say it.

ToolLine.title: ToolLine
ToolLine.description:
One tool the agent called: its name, a line a person reads, whether it worked, and the
refusal when it did not (#463). `running` while the tool has not returned (#504): its label
says what is happening now.

TurnState.title: TurnState
TurnState.description:
Whether an assistant turn has landed.

A user turn appears immediately and its answer arrives later, so the transcript holds a turn
that exists and has no content yet. Two booleans would make `pending and failed`
representable; three members do not.

UpstreamTool.title: UpstreamTool
UpstreamTool.description: One tool the module wraps, from `meta.yml`'s `tools`.

Urgency.title: Urgency
Urgency.description: How much a thing costs if it waits.

ValueSource.title: ValueSource
ValueSource.description: Identify who or what settled a value, independently of its resolution tier.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description: A complete collection of validation findings.

Where.title: Where
Where.description: Persistence boundary for a setting; browser values never reach the server.
